To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a given citation can have different weights, depending on the previous achievements of the author quoting a given paper.

the weighted number of citation is the weighted average number of citation, the weighted impact factor of journal is the weighted average impact factor of the journals citing the journal, the Hirsch index of a scientist is the number of the most highly weighted papers published by this scientist, and the Hirsch index is the number of most highly weighted papers, published by scientists working in this institution.

the citation graph of a given scientific institution, defined by the matrix of citation relations between its members, has a unique normalized eigenvector with positive components, and the components of this eigenvector are the weighting factors of the corresponding authors, reflecting the scientific achievements of all authors quoting the work of these authors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of the evaluation of the impact of a scientific work.

a quantitative description of the citation network, with a possibility to define the impact of a paper in the network, and with a definition of the impact of a given scientist in a given field of science.
a problem of defining a measure of the scientific output of an individual scientist and a scientific journal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed scheme allows us to introduce a quantitative measure of scientific impact of a given paper.

the proposed method of evaluation of scientific output is a natural extension of the existing citation-based methods, and it provides a better and more accurate picture of a given scientist's or institution's achievements.

the proposed scheme of evaluation allows us to distinguish between a number of citations and their quality, i.e. to take into account the scientific achievements of other scientists who quote a given paper.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the weighted Hirsch index, which is a measure of an individual scientific performance, is a better measure than the H-index.
the weighted impact factors and the weighted Hirsch indices are more appropriate for evaluation of a scientific output than the standard ones.
a citation graph is a powerful tool to describe the scientific achievements of individual scientists, journals and entire institutions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the weighting factor of the authors is a measure of the scientific importance of a given author.
, in the context of the scientific evaluation, it is crucial to take into consideration not only number of citations of a given paper or a scientist but also the quality of these citations.

the weighted impact factors and Hirsch indices are better suited to measure the impact of a scientific paper or a journal than the classical ones, because the former take into account the scientific achievements of the authors of citing papers.
